+# Contributing
+
+Thanks for helping out. This is a small project, so the process is short.
+
+## Before you start
+
+- For anything beyond a typo, open an issue first and describe the change you
+  want to make. Agreeing on the approach up front is cheaper than reworking a
+  finished branch.
+- Check open issues and pull requests so two people don't build the same thing.
+
+## Making a change
+
+1. Create a branch off `main`, named for the change (`fix-readme-links`, not
+   `patch-1`).
+2. Keep the branch scoped to one change. Unrelated cleanups belong in their own
+   branch — they make review slower and bisects less useful.
+3. Commit in logical steps. Each commit should leave the repository in a working
+   state.
+
+## Commit messages
+
+Use a short imperative subject line (under ~72 characters), then a blank line,
+then the body if the change needs explanation:
+
+```
+Add contributing notes
+
+The README pointed at guidelines that did not exist. Document how to
+propose and review changes so contributors do not have to guess.
+```
+
+Explain *why* in the body. The diff already shows *what*.
+
+## Pull requests
+
+- Describe what changed and why, and link the issue it addresses.
+- Say how you verified the change. If you could not verify it, say that too —
+  an honest gap is more useful than an implied guarantee.
+- Expect at least one review before merge. Address comments with follow-up
+  commits rather than force-pushing over the reviewed history; squash on merge
+  if the history is noisy.
+
+## Building and testing
+
+This project currently has no build system, test suite, or CI. If your change
+introduces code, introduce the tooling to exercise it in the same pull request,
+and update this section to describe how to run it. Please don't add code that
+has no way to be checked.
+
+## Reporting bugs
+
+Open an issue with:
+
+- what you did,
+- what you expected,
+- what happened instead,
+- the version or commit you were on.
+
+## Code of conduct
+
+Be straightforward and civil. Review the change, not the person who wrote it.
